s2.title: Why Not Use div Instead?
s2.li1: Screen readers recognize semantic tags for better accessibility
s2.li2: Search engines understand content structure more accurately
s2.li3: Code readability and maintainability are greatly improved

a2.title: Flexbox Layout Practical Techniques
a2.intro: Flexbox is the core tool for modern CSS layout. Mastering these property combinations solves 90% of layout needs.

s2.title: Practical Case Analysis
s2.p1: In the footer layout, we use flex + stretch for equal height, flex-shrink:0 to protect the QR code, and min-width:0 + overflow-wrap to prevent narrow-screen overflow.
s2.p2: Combining these properties with media queries covers most business scenarios.

a3.title: Core Principles of Responsive Design
a3.intro: The goal of responsive design is to provide a good user experience on any device, from 320px phones to 2560px ultrawide monitors.

s1.title: Mobile-First Strategy
s1.p1: Mobile-first means writing mobile styles as the base, then progressively enhancing for desktop via min-width media queries.
s1.li1: Base styles → Apply to all screens

s2.title: Breakpoint Selection & Content Adaptation
s2.p1: Breakpoints should be based on when content 'breaks', not specific devices.
s2.p2: Common breakpoints: 480px (large phone), 768px (tablet), 1024px (small desktop), 1200px (standard desktop). Adjust based on design.
